newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ninth body found from Japan mudslide, five missing.
newsitem.headline: Ninth body found from Japan mudslide, five missing.

text.p: Searchers recovered a ninth body and looked for five workers still missing and feared dead on Monday after a mudslide buried a mountain road construction site in central Japan last week, police said.
In chilly weather and amid fears of a second mudslide, the searchers used sniffer dogs to scour for the missing workers near Otari village in Nagano Prefecture, 230 km (140 miles) northwest of Tokyo.
The mudslide tore through a steep river valley on Friday morning after rains melted heavy accumulations of snow.
Of the 20 workers caught in the mudslide, six were rescued.
The missing and dead were among a crew of about 50 who were restoring an embankment damaged in a 1995 landslide.
The accident occurred in a ski resort and hot spring spa area, a region of steep, rugged mountains prone to landslides.
Otari is 10 km (six miles) from one of the main ski slopes to be used in the 1998 Winter Olympics at Nagano.
Police said the highway restoration project was not connected with preparations for the Games.
